title: Privileged mintFor() and burn() ignore the global `paused` flag and per-index `disabled` flag — NFT supply keeps changing during an emergency pause and for disabled indexes (NFTMigrator interaction)
description: Only the paid `mint()`/`_executeMint()` path is gated by `require(!paused)` and `require(!config.disabled)` (lines 171/174). The two privileged supply-changing entry points are not: `mintFor(index,recipient)` (line 206) checks only `authorizedMinters[msg.sender]` and `configs[index].dispatcher != 0`, and `burn(holder,tokenId,quantity)` (line 341) checks only `authorizedBurners[msg.sender]`. Neither consults `paused` nor `config.disabled`. The Global-Pauser integration (`pause()`/`unpause()`, gated to `pauser`) and the per-index kill switch (`setDispatcherDisabled`) therefore do NOT halt NFT issuance/burning through these roles. This is the interaction-level realisation of Tier-1 LOCAL-NMV2-001 / SA-017 / SA-018: the only wired authorized minter in the design is NFTMigrator, so `migrate()` can keep minting V2 claim NFTs (via mintFor) while the contract is paused, and can mint for a V2 index the owner has explicitly disabled.
exploitPathOrPreconditions: Precondition: an authorized minter or burner is set (per trust assumption #6 the NFTMigrator is wired as authorizedMinter on V2). (a) Pauser pauses NFTMinterV2 to halt activity during an incident; an authorized minter (or any user driving NFTMigrator.migrate()) can still mint claim NFTs via mintFor — emergency pause is not a complete stop. (b) Owner disables index X via setDispatcherDisabled (documented as 'new mints are blocked'); paid mint(X) reverts, but mintFor(X) (and migrate() mapping V1->X) still mints index X. No untrusted party gains anything beyond what the trusted minter/burner already could, and migrator mints are 1:1 against burned V1 NFTs (no net claim inflation), which is why this is Low rather than higher.
impact: Operational/footgun + spec deviation: the pauser/owner reasonably expects `paused` to stop all minting and `disabled` to block all new issuance of that index, but privileged paths bypass both. No direct loss; supply still 1:1-backed in the migration case.
lawNotes: Reported as a non-obvious owner/pauser footgun (Law 3 in-scope) and for Law-1 recall — not a malicious-owner vector. Pauser/owner *trust* is OOS, but the incompleteness of the pause *mechanism* is a code-coverage gap, surfaced at honest (Low) severity.
recommendation: If the intent is a privileged escape hatch, document it explicitly; otherwise add `require(!paused)` to mintFor (and consider burn) and `require(!configs[index].disabled)` to mintFor so the kill switches are honored uniformly across mint(), mintFor() and burn().

title: replaceDispatcher() carries the old per-index price to a new dispatcher whose primeToken() may differ — subsequent mint() charges a stale, possibly mis-scaled price in a different token
rootCauseClass: config carry-over across a dispatcher swap with a different prime token
description: replaceDispatcher swaps `configs[index].dispatcher`, `dispatcherToIndex`, and `tokenIdToDispatcher`, but preserves `configs[index].price`/`growthBasisPoints`. In V2 the charged token is read at mint time from `ITokenDispatcherV2(config.dispatcher).primeToken()` (H-01 fix, line 177), so the SAME numeric `price` is now interpreted in the NEW dispatcher's prime-token units. If the replacement dispatcher's primeToken has different decimals or value than the old one (e.g. swapping an 18-dp USDS dispatcher for a 6-dp token dispatcher), the carried-over price is silently mis-scaled — over- or under-charging the next minters until the owner notices and calls setPrice. This is the interaction-level form of LOCAL-NMV2-003 / pattern C-01: the cross-contract coupling is that the price field lives in NFTMinterV2 while its denomination is defined by whichever dispatcher is currently bound to the index.
exploitPathOrPreconditions: Owner replaces the dispatcher at an index with one whose primeToken differs in decimals/value and forgets to re-set price. Next paid mint() pulls `price` units of the new token. No external attacker; this is an owner footgun. Bounded by owner-trust, hence Low.
impact: Minters charged a wrong amount (potential over/under-payment) for the window between replaceDispatcher and a corrective setPrice. No fund custody change beyond the mispriced payment.
lawNotes: Non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3 in-scope): replaceDispatcher's name suggests a like-for-like swap and does not hint that price persists and is re-denominated. Surfaced with safe-config guidance, not as a malicious-owner vector.
recommendation: Document the carry-over loudly, or have replaceDispatcher require an explicit new price argument (or reset price to 0 / re-emit PriceUpdated) so the operator must reconfirm the price against the new primeToken.

title: REFUTED — Cross-contract reentrancy via the PSM self-call (try this._psmDonate{}) under the dispatch nonReentrant lock
description: `try this._psmDonate(remaining)` executes while the base `dispatch` holds the OZ ReentrancyGuard lock. _psmDonate is `require(msg.sender == address(this))` and calls ISkyPSM.buyGem(). A re-entrant PSM cannot reach any unguarded state-changing path: dispatch() and pool() are nonReentrant (lock held), unlockCallback requires msg.sender==_vault, _psmDonate is self-gated, and every state mutator is onlyOwner. The approve+buyGem+approve(0) sequence is fully INSIDE the self-call, so a buyGem revert atomically rolls back the approval (caught by the outer try/catch -> USDS parks) with no dangling allowance. Reentrancy containment confirmed; LOCAL-BPV2-003 closed.
exploitPathOrPreconditions: Would require the canonical Sky PSM (semi-trusted) to be malicious AND a reachable unguarded write — neither exists.

title: REFUTED — Unchecked return values of buyGem (SA-001), sUSDS.deposit (SA-002), addLiquidity/settle (SA-004/005)
description: Each ignored return is non-load-bearing. buyGem: the contract PRE-COMPUTES `usdsSpent` and forceApprove()s exactly that, then resets to 0; buyGem delivers exactly `gemAmt` USDC to batchMinter or reverts — the returned usdsInWad is informational. sUSDS.deposit: shares minted are not relied upon; pool() re-reads `balanceOf(sUSDS)`. settle/addLiquidity: settle amount is the measured `actualInVault` balance-delta; only bptAmountOut is needed and is checked against minBPT inside addLiquidity. No short-fill or interface-drift creates an exploitable state given the balance-delta re-reads. Defensive hardening only, not a vuln.

title: REFUTED — div-before-mul precision loss in _psmDonate (SA-009)
rootCauseClass: n/a (rounding favors protocol, matches PSM math)
description: gemAmt = floor(usdsAmount*WAD/(conv*(WAD+tout))); usdsSpent = gemAmt*conv*(WAD+tout)/WAD. Because gemAmt is floored, usdsSpent <= usdsAmount always (never over-spends the swept USDS; remainder parks as dust). The recomputed usdsSpent equals the live PSM's pull exactly: PSM computes gemAmt*conv + floor(gemAmt*conv*tout/WAD), and gemAmt*conv*(WAD+tout)/WAD = gemAmt*conv + floor(gemAmt*conv*tout/WAD) since gemAmt*conv*WAD/WAD is exact. So the approval is neither short (would revert buyGem -> caught -> park) nor excess (reset to 0 after). require(gemAmt>0) bounces sub-unit donations into the park path. Internally consistent and PSM-faithful.

title: REFUTED — Cross-index reentrancy break via ERC1155 receiver hook in NFTMinterV2._executeMint (Ledger L-01)
description: `config.price` is bumped (line 188) BEFORE both external interactions (dispatch at 191, _mint at 196). The onERC1155Received callback fires after the price effect and after dispatch's nonReentrant lock has been released. A re-entrant mint() — same or different index — is a fresh, fully-validated mint that pulls payment from the re-entering caller, bumps that index's price, dispatches, and mints. No stale-price window: re-entering the same index reads the already-incremented price. Re-entering the same dispatcher's dispatch hits its nonReentrant guard only while dispatch is on the stack; by callback time it is not. No cross-index invariant break exists.
exploitPathOrPreconditions: None; any re-entry requires fresh payment at the current (already-grown) price.

title: REFUTED — Double-mint / mis-accounting via reentrancy in NFTMigrator.migrate (SA-020)
description: Within each index iteration the V1 balance is read, then v1.burn(...) executes BEFORE the inner v2.mintFor() loop. If the caller (ERC1155 receiver = msg.sender) re-enters migrate() during a mintFor callback, every already-processed index has V1 balance 0 (burned) and is skipped, while not-yet-processed indexes are fully migrated by the re-entrant call and then skipped by the outer loop. Net result is exactly one V2 mint per burned V1 unit regardless of re-entry ordering. No double-credit. (Gas-DoS on large holders remains Ledger M-01/M-02, wont-fix: migration already executed; no new evidence it is live, so not re-escalated.)
exploitPathOrPreconditions: None for double-mint; the only residual is the known unbounded-loop gas exhaustion (already triaged wont-fix).

title: REFUTED — Balancer V3 unlock/addLiquidity/settle amount mismatch & callback reentrancy (Lead B)
rootCauseClass: n/a (slippage is operator-supplied; settle matches measured transfer)
description: unlockCallback is gated to msg.sender==_vault and is only reachable via pool()'s nonReentrant unlock. settle() is passed `actualInVault` = measured balance-delta of the sUSDS transferred to the vault, and addLiquidity maxAmountsIn uses the same measured value with `_sUSDSIsFirst` ordering set by the owner — internally consistent for a non-FOT sUSDS. The `minBPT` slippage floor is supplied by the authorized (trusted) pooler with no on-chain reference; that MEV/sandwich exposure is a value/MEV concern routed to econ-scanner, not a code defect. No reentrancy or amount-matching bug at the code level.
exploitPathOrPreconditions: minBPT=0 sandwich is an operator-discipline/econ matter (pattern rank-1), deferred to econ-scanner.

title: DEFERRED to econ-scanner — Full-balance USDS donation sweep vs gross-amount phUSD mint-debt asymmetry, and uncapped phUSD pull
description: The donation sweeps the FULL USDS balance (this dispatch's share + any stranded USDS), shipping USDC to batchMinter, while hook.onDispatch accrues phUSD mint-debt on the GROSS per-dispatch `amount` only (LOCAL-BPV2-004). Two independent percentages (batchDonationSize for USDC out vs hook.ratio for phUSD debt) couple here, and BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.pull() mints phUSD equal to the uncapped accrued mintDebt. setRatio allows ratio==50 (and the default is 50) despite docs stating strictly <50 (LOCAL-HOOK-001 / L-02 — an off-by-one in the cap, owner-set and economic). Whether minted phUSD is collateral-backed against pooled sUSDS / donated USDC is a solvency question. No code-level exploit; routed to econ-scanner (and noted as DEDUP-001 unbacked-phUSD economics).
